chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When you are present with the dying person before he dies, then prompt him with the shahādah that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the dying person being attended before death
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: the testimony of faith to be uttered
key_terms.عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ: description of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as Allah’s servant and Messenger
key_terms.فَلَقِّنْهُ: prompt him to recite or repeat
key_terms.لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ: affirmation that Allah has no partner

ai.seo_question: What should be recited to a dying person before death in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that when one is present with a person at the approach of death, one should prompt him to recite the shahādah. It reflects the importance of affirming tawhid and the messengership of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم at the final moments of life.
